learn.title: Reading a line safely
learn.body: To read a line of text, use `fgets(buffer, size, stdin)`. It reads at most `size - 1` characters, always adds the terminator, and so never writes past the end of your buffer. That makes it the safe tool.

learn.title: Read one line
learn.body: `sizeof line` is the buffer size, 20. The input `hi` plus Enter is read as `hi` and the newline. The output shows the newline inside the brackets.

learn.title: fgets keeps the newline
learn.body: The Enter key is part of the line, so the string ends with `'\n'`. If the line is too long for the buffer, only the first part is read and the rest waits for the next call.

learn.title: Remove the newline
learn.body: `strcspn(line, "\n")` returns the index of the first newline, or the length if there is none. Setting that slot to the terminator cuts it off. It prints `[hi]`.

learn.title: Read until the end
learn.body: `fgets` returns `NULL` at the end of input, so a `while` loop reads every line. With two lines of input it prints 2.

steps: It adds the terminator in slot 3

learn.body: Avoid `gets`, it cannot limit the length and was removed in C11. `scanf("%s")` has no limit either, unless you give one.

questions.prompt: What does `fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin)` do?
choices: Reads one line, at most the buffer size
questions.explanation: It stops at a newline or when the buffer is nearly full.

questions.prompt: `char line[20];` With `fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin)`, how many characters can it read at most? Type the number.
questions.explanation: One slot is kept for the terminator.

questions.prompt: What does `fgets` return at the end of the input?
`fgets` keeps the \_\_ at the end of the line.
questions.explanation: The Enter key becomes `'\n'` in the string.
`strcspn` finds where the newline sits, and a terminator cuts the string there.

choices: It cannot limit how much it writes
questions.explanation: A long line overruns the buffer. It was removed in C11.

questions.prompt: The input is `hello`, the buffer is `char b[4]`. What does the first `fgets` store?
questions.explanation: At most 3 characters, plus the terminator.
